- HIL results carry the firmware hash and the SHAs of all pinned repos ([*HIL results carry the firmw... (XD-RULE-0012)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0012),
  [*HIL results carry firmware ... (XD-CHECK-0005)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0005)).
- Evidence counts only from commits on `main` or baseline tags ([*Evidence only from main or ... (XD-ADR-0053)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0053)). Runs on PR
  branches are previews.
- A result whose SHAs no longer match the pins is stale and doesn’t count ([*Only valid evidence counts (XD-RULE-0013)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0013),
  [*stale evidence (R5a) (XD-CHECK-0011)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0011)).
- Every requirement needs a `verifies` link ([*Every requirement is verified (XD-RULE-0009)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0009), [*every requirement verified ... (XD-CHECK-0007)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0007)).

#### NOTE
The run-record schema and the extraction of `TR` needs from test reports are being
built (task 4.5a). Until then, test reports show the sphinx-test-reports needs.

## Checks

```sh
curatrix check robarm-integration --stage local
```


# howto/add-a-view.html.md

<a id="howto-add-a-view"></a>

# Add a view

Use this guide when you want a diagram of the model in the docs. Views come from the model:
nobody draws model content by hand ([*Views as drawio files rende... (XD-ADR-0002)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0002), [*View definitions live in th... (XD-ADR-0085)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0085)).

## Steps

1. Define the view in `model/views.sysml` as a SysML `view` with `@XdView` metadata. Its
   short name is a `SYS-VIEW` ID, a reserved kind that is not a need:
   ```text
   view <'SYS-VIEW-NEW-joint'> jointView {
       @XdView { kind = "interconnection"; root = "RobArm::JointModule"; }
       expose RobArm::JointModule::**;
   }
   ```
2. Issue the ID and build the view:
   ```sh
   curatrix ids fix robarm-syseng
   curatrix gen model robarm-syseng
   curatrix views build robarm-syseng --view jointView
   ```

   This writes `views/jointView.drawio.svg`: the picture with the drawio diagram embedded
   ([*Views are committed as edit... (XD-ADR-0087)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0087)). Commit it.
3. Show it in a document:
   ```rst
   .. sysml-view:: /views/jointView.drawio.svg
      :caption: Joint module
   ```

   The document’s `conf.py` must list `(REPO, "views/*.drawio.svg")` in `generated`.
4. Optional: arrange the boxes by hand.
   ```sh
   curatrix launch drawio robarm-syseng/views/jointView.drawio.svg
   curatrix views normalize robarm-syseng/views/jointView.drawio.svg
   ```

   Layout is not model content. The check compares content, not geometry ([*Small corrections from rese... (XD-ADR-0057)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0057) (a)).

## Checks

- [*views match the model (cont... (XD-CHECK-0018)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0018): content matches the model, the diagram is uncompressed, geometry is sane and
  the picture is fresh. It needs no browser.
-  [*.FCStd uncompressed; drawio... (XD-CHECK-0025)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0025): no compressed diagrams ([*Design files are stored unc... (XD-RULE-0039)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0039)).

#### NOTE
Iteration 1 builds the view kinds `interconnection` and `decomposition`.
`context`, `usecases`, `allocation` and `variants` come later. Keeping manual layout
across rebuilds is iteration 2 ([*Scope moved to iteration 2 (XD-ADR-0037)*](explanation/decisions/scope.html.md#XD-ADR-0037)). Trace graphs use `needflow`, not drawio
([*Trace graphs with needflow (XD-ADR-0086)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0086)).

## Pitfalls

- `views build` needs node, elkjs and Firefox. They are installed by the bootstrap; it runs
  locally only.
- After saving in drawio, always run `views normalize`. The pre-commit hook insists.


# howto/cross-repo-change.html.md

<a id="howto-cross-repo-change"></a>

# Make a change across repos

Use this guide when one change touches more than one repo, for example a new system requirement
plus the domain requirements and design that follow from it.

## Steps

1. **One branch name** for the change, in every repo it touches ([*One branch name across repos (XD-ADR-0045)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0045)), e.g.
   `feat/latency`. Work in a worktree set, so the main checkouts stay untouched
   ([*Parallel agents work in git... (XD-ADR-0114)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0114)):
   ```sh
   curatrix work start feat/latency robarm-syseng robarm-sw
   cd .worktrees/feat/latency
   ```

   Builds of the set go to `build/wt-feat-latency/`.

   #### NOTE
   `curatrix work` is being added (task 4.4c). Until it is on `main`, make the
   worktrees by hand: `git -C <repo> worktree add ../.worktrees/<branch>/<repo> -b <branch>`.
2. **Author** the change in each repo, run `curatrix gen` and `curatrix ids fix` where
   needed.
3. **Check every repo you touched**, with CAD content where the repo has it ([*Every check also runs locally (XD-ADR-0040)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0040)):
   ```sh
   curatrix check robarm-syseng --stage local
   curatrix check robarm-sw --stage local
   ```
4. **Open one PR per repo.** Each PR lists its sibling PRs and the affected needs, and ends with
   the provenance trailer ([*Provenance trailer on GitHu... (XD-ADR-0065)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0065)).
5. **PR CI** checks each repo without CAD content ([*CI runs without CAD content (XD-ADR-0049)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0049)). For sibling repos it uses, in
   this order: a branch with the same name; the repo’s `main` if the manifest pin is an
   ancestor of it; the manifest pin ([*PR CI sibling resolution (XD-ADR-0116)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0116)).
6. **Merge upstream first**: syseng, then the domains, then integration. Framework changes merge
   before the repos that use them. Every PR is rebase-merged ([*Trunk-based merging with re... (XD-ADR-0043)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0043)).
7. **Bump.** The bump bot in the manifest repo collects the new `main` SHAs into one bump PR and
   builds the full set ([*A bump bot for manifest pins (XD-ADR-0054)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0054), [*The bump bot is a scheduled... (XD-ADR-0081)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0081)). Merging it moves the pins ([*The manifest is the only pl... (XD-ADR-0033)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0033)).
8. When everything is merged:
   ```sh
   curatrix work done feat/latency
   ```

## Roles

The bootstrap’s role decides which repos you have. A role always includes its upstream repos and
the framework ([*West submanifests and proje... (XD-ADR-0079)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0079)).

| Role               | Group filter               | You get                                                                                                                                |
|--------------------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `syseng` (default) | (manifest default)         | framework, syseng, libraries, Zephyr                                                                                                   |
| `ee` / `ee3d`      | `+ee` / `+ee,+kicad-3d`    | plus the EE repo and KiCad libraries (with 3D models)                                                                                  |
| `me`               | `+me,+freecad-parts`       | plus the ME repo and the FreeCAD parts library                                                                                         |
| `sw`               | `+sw`                      | plus the SW repo                                                                                                                       |
| `integration`      | `+ee,+me,+sw,+integration` | every repo without the big libraries ([*The integration role (XD-ADR-0082)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0082)) |
| `full`             | all groups                 | everything                                                                                                                             |

## Pitfalls

- `west update` moves repos back to their pins (detached HEAD). On branches use
  `curatrix update`. Never run either inside a worktree set.
- A ledger conflict after a rebase means two PRs issued the same ID. Rerun `curatrix ids fix`.


# howto/index.html.md

<a id="howto-index"></a>

# How-to guides

Each guide answers one question: “How do I …?”. It assumes you have a workspace
([Your first workspace](tutorials/first-workspace.html.md)) and know the basic ideas. All commands run from the
workspace root.

* [Add a requirement](howto/add-a-requirement.html.md)
* [Add a model element](howto/add-a-model-element.html.md)
* [Add a view](howto/add-a-view.html.md)
* [Add a PCBA or circuit block](howto/add-a-pcba.html.md)
* [Add a FreeCAD part or assembly](howto/add-a-part.html.md)
* [Add a feature or configuration](howto/add-a-configuration.html.md)
* [Add a test](howto/add-a-test.html.md)
* [Make a change across repos](howto/cross-repo-change.html.md)
* [Work as an agent](howto/work-as-an-agent.html.md)
* [Make a baseline](howto/make-a-baseline.html.md)


# howto/make-a-baseline.html.md

<a id="howto-make-a-baseline"></a>

# Make a baseline

Use this guide when you want a fixed, released set of repo versions. A **baseline** is a tag
`baseline/vX.Y.Z` of the manifest repo; a **bundle** is the package of outputs built from it
([*Terms: baseline and bundle (XD-ADR-0034)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0034), [*SemVer tags and baseline tags (XD-ADR-0047)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0047)).

## Steps

1. Merge the open bump PR, so the manifest pins the latest `main` of every repo.
2. Use a workspace with the `full` role, so all CAD content is there ([*CI runs without CAD content (XD-ADR-0049)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0049)).
3. Run the baseline gates for every repo, then the full set:
   ```sh
   curatrix check robarm-syseng --stage baseline --base <last-baseline-needs>
   curatrix check robarm-manifest --stage baseline --base <last-baseline-needs>
   ```

   `--base` points at the `needs.json` files of the last baseline.
4. Fix what fails. The baseline stage is stricter than `local` and `pr`:
   - [*no links to retired needs (... (XD-CHECK-0008)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0008): links to retired needs fail now; the grace period ends ([*Links to retired needs are ... (XD-RULE-0011)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0011),
     [*A grace period for retired ... (XD-ADR-0068)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0068)).
   - [*suspect links against the l... (XD-CHECK-0024)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0024): open suspect links fail ([*Suspect links are reviewed ... (XD-RULE-0014)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0014)).
   - [*generated files record the ... (XD-CHECK-0020)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0020): generated files must record the pinned tool versions.
   - [*stale evidence (R5a) (XD-CHECK-0011)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0011): stale evidence doesn’t count ([*Only valid evidence counts (XD-RULE-0013)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0013)).
   - [*every requirement verified ... (XD-CHECK-0007)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0007): missing verification is a warning in iteration 1 ([*Verification coverage is a ... (XD-ADR-0090)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0090)).
5. Tag the manifest repo with an annotated tag and push it:
   ```sh
   git -C robarm-manifest tag -a baseline/v0.1.0 -m "baseline v0.1.0"
   git -C robarm-manifest push origin baseline/v0.1.0
   ```
6. Create the GitHub release. Its assets are the outputs (docs, later CAM data and firmware).

#### NOTE
Bundles, CAM output and PDF documents come in iteration 2 ([*Scope moved to iteration 2 (XD-ADR-0037)*](explanation/decisions/scope.html.md#XD-ADR-0037)). The docs of
each baseline are hosted next to `main` on Pages ([*Docs hosting on GitHub Page... (XD-ADR-0048)*](explanation/decisions/documents.html.md#XD-ADR-0048)); multi-version hosting is
still being built.

## Pitfalls

- Tombstones in `generated/retired-needs.json` are dropped at the next baseline. Remove the
  links to them before you tag.
- Only a person makes baselines. Agents may prepare the gate results.


# howto/work-as-an-agent.html.md

<a id="howto-work-as-an-agent"></a>

# Work as an agent

Use this guide if you are an AI agent, or if you brief one. Agents do the same work with the same
tools as people ([*Agents are first-class (XD-ADR-0003)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0003)). The differences are listed here.

## Before you start

1. Read the workspace `CLAUDE.md` (copied from `xdmod/launch/CLAUDE.md`, [*Agent material in each repo... (XD-ADR-0062)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0062)) and
   the `claude/CLAUDE.md` of each repo you change.
2. Get a brief: goal, binding decisions, files to read, output paths, and what you must not do.
3. Work in your own worktree set ([*Parallel agents work in git... (XD-ADR-0114)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0114)): `curatrix work start <branch> <repos...>`.
   One agent per branch per repo.

## What agents may and may not do

| Agents may                                                                                                                                                                       | Agents may not                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| create branches, commit, push to their own branches                                                                                                                              | merge PRs, push to `main`, force-push to other people’s branches                                                                                                                                     |
| open PRs and issues and comment on them, with the provenance trailer ([*Provenance trailer on GitHu... (XD-ADR-0065)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0065)) | change repo or org settings without the owner’s approval of the concrete action list<br/>([*GitHub admin by agents only... (XD-ADR-0112)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0112)) |
| add `Co-Authored-By`, and `Signed-off-by` where a repo requires it ([*Sign-off by agents (XD-ADR-0108)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0108))               | affirm suspect links or give manual verdicts; they only propose them ([*Only a human's commit affirms (XD-ADR-0051)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0051))                      |
| run any tool through curatrix, under limits ([*A memory limit and a timeou... (XD-ADR-0064)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0064))                          | run tools without limits, install system packages, use sudo                                                                                                                                          |
| post freely in the framework and project repos                                                                                                                                   | post on other repos before the owner approved the draft ([*Posting approval outside ou... (XD-ADR-0113)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0113))                                  |

## Rules while working

- Run every command from the workspace root ([*All commands run from the w... (XD-ADR-0060)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0060)). Run tools that curatrix has no
  subcommand for through `curatrix run -- <cmd>` ([*Every tool runs under limits (XD-RULE-0044)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0044)).
- Write placeholder IDs and run `curatrix ids fix`; never invent numbers ([*No placeholders on main (XD-RULE-0017)*](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0017)).
- Put build output only under `build/<area>/` ([*Build output only under build/ (XD-RULE-0040)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0040)).
- Every commit ends with `Co-Authored-By: <agent> <noreply@anthropic.com>` ([*Agents work under the user'... (XD-ADR-0044)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0044),
  [*Agent commits carry a trailer (XD-RULE-0042)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0042)). Everything posted on GitHub ends with the provenance trailer.
- Run `curatrix check <repo> --stage local` for every repo you touched before you push.
- Every PR gets a review by another agent before the owner’s review ([*Every PR gets an agent review (XD-ADR-0115)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0115)).

## Skills and checklists

The bootstrap links skills and commands from `xdmod/claude/` and each active repo’s
`claude/` folder into `<workspace>/.claude/` ([*The bootstrap assembles .cl... (XD-ADR-0103)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0103)).

#### NOTE
The SYSMOD step skills, the review checklists and commands such as `/review-pr` are
written in Phase 5.

## Pitfalls

- Agents use the owner’s login. The limits above are policy, not technical enforcement, in
  iteration 1 ([*Agent limits are policy onl... (XD-ADR-0123)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0123)).


# reference/checks.html.md

<a id="ref-checks"></a>

# Checks

curatrix runs every check with one command per repo, from the workspace root ([*Every check runs locally (XD-RULE-0032)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0032)):

```sh
curatrix check <repo> [--stage local|pr|full|baseline] [--no-cad] [--only IDs] [--json]
```

The check catalogue on this page is generated from curatrix. Each check is also a need
(`XD-CHECK`) that enforces one or more method rules; see [Check needs]() at the end.

## Stages

| Stage      | Who runs it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Scope                                                                                                                                                       | CAD content   | Purpose                                   |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `local`    | a person or agent, one command per repo ([*Every check also runs locally (XD-ADR-0040)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0040)), under limits ([*A memory limit and a timeou... (XD-ADR-0064)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0064)) | the repo and its upstream documents                                                                                                                         | yes           | full feedback before pushing              |
| pre-commit | git hooks, installed by the bootstrap ([*Pre-commit hooks (XD-ADR-0091)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0091)); staged files only                                                                                                                       | changed files                                                                                                                                               | no            | normalizers, placeholder IDs, fast checks |
| `pr`       | GitHub Actions per repo ([*GitHub CI builds docs and r... (XD-ADR-0041)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0041), [*CI runs without CAD content (XD-ADR-0049)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0049))                                  | the repo and its siblings on the same branch name ([*One branch name across repos (XD-ADR-0045)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0045)) | no            | gate for merging                          |
| `full`     | the bump-bot job in the manifest repo ([*The bump bot is a scheduled... (XD-ADR-0081)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0081))                                                                                                                            | all repos at the new pins                                                                                                                                   | no            | cross-repo rules                          |
| `baseline` | a person, locally, before tagging `baseline/vX.Y.Z`                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | all repos, full checkout                                                                                                                                    | yes           | release quality                           |

GitHub CI runs `--stage pr --no-cad`. Checks that need KiCad, FreeCAD or the SysML Pilot run
locally ([*CI runs without CAD content (XD-ADR-0049)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0049)). The committed CAD-derived needs let CI still see the full trace graph
([*CAD-derived needs are commi... (XD-ADR-0100)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0100)).

## Levels

- **error**: the finding fails the stage.
- **warning**: the finding is reported but does not fail.
- **report**: the finding adds a summary, for example to a PR.

(XD-RULE-0043)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0043)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Domain checks

Repos add their own checks as `commands` in their `checks.yaml`. They are not curatrix
checks and have no `XD-CHECK` need. Typical domain checks compare domain content with the
interfaces in the systems engineering repo: a KiCad netlist against the pin maps, the Zephyr
devicetree against the model, FreeCAD parameters against model attributes, KiCad ERC and FreeCAD
recompute, the firmware build and unit tests.

## Output

- Logs and a summary go to `build/<area>/checks/`. The summary JSON
  (`build/<area>/checks/summary.json`, also printed with `--json`) lists every check with its
  status (`pass`, `fail`, `warn`, `report`, `skip`), findings, log and reproduce command.
- For every failure, curatrix prints the command that reproduces it.
- A stage fails when any check has the status `fail`.

The format of `checks.yaml` is in the curatrix reference.

## Check needs

<a id="XD-CHECK-0001"></a>

Run it alone: `curatrix check <repo> --only CK-H5`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |


# reference/glossary.html.md

<a id="ref-glossary"></a>

# Glossary

<a id="term-150-model"></a>

150 % model
: The product architecture with all variation points and all their variants. Each
  configuration picks one variant per variation point. See [Variants](explanation/variants.html.md).

<a id="term-affirmation"></a>

affirmation
: A person’s confirmation that a suspect link is still correct. Agents may propose it; only a
  person’s commit counts.

<a id="term-affirmatrix"></a>

affirmatrix
: The suspect-link tool that XDMOD will use once it is adapted.

<a id="term-area"></a>

area
: The folder under `build/` that a build writes to: the repo name, `full` for the full
  set, the branch for worktree builds, or a named step.

<a id="term-backlink"></a>

backlink
: The reverse direction of a trace link, for example “verified by”. Backlinks are never
  written; the tools compute them.

<a id="term-baseline"></a>

baseline
: A tag `baseline/vX.Y.Z` of the manifest repo: a fixed set of repo versions. The baseline
  gates run before it is tagged.

<a id="term-bump-bot"></a>

bump bot
: A scheduled job in the manifest repo that moves the pins to the repos’ `main` and opens
  one bump PR.

<a id="term-bundle"></a>

bundle
: The package of outputs built from one baseline: documents, CAM data, firmware, HIL
  results. Iteration 2.

<a id="term-configuration"></a>

configuration
: One product of a product line: a choice of features with one product model. ID kind
  `SYS-CFG`.

<a id="term-curatrix"></a>

curatrix
: XDMOD’s command-line tool. It runs checks, generators, ID issuing, views, docs builds,
  bootstrap and launchers, every tool under limits.

<a id="term-EARS"></a>

EARS
: Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax: sentence patterns for requirements, such as “When
  <trigger>, the system shall <response>.”

<a id="term-evidence-branch"></a>

evidence branch
: An orphan branch in the integration repo that holds HIL run records. It is never merged.

<a id="term-feature"></a>

feature
: A property that distinguishes products of a product line, in the feature model. ID kind
  `SYS-FEAT`.

<a id="term-full-set"></a>

full set
: All documents of a project, built together from one workspace by the manifest repo.

<a id="term-generated-need"></a>

generated need
: A need extracted from a source (SysML, KiCad, FreeCAD, code, test results) instead of
  written in rst. It follows the same rules as authored needs.

<a id="term-HIL"></a>

HIL
: Hardware in the loop: tests that run firmware on real hardware.

<a id="term-ledger"></a>

ledger
: The file `ids.yaml` in each repo. It lists every ID number ever issued per kind.

<a id="term-manifest-repo"></a>

manifest repo
: The repo with the west manifest. It is the only place that pins revisions.

<a id="term-need"></a>

need
: An item managed by sphinx-needs, with an ID, a type, fields and links: a requirement, a
  design element, a test case, a decision, a rule.

<a id="term-placeholder"></a>

placeholder
: A temporary ID of the form `<KIND>-NEW-<tag>`. `curatrix ids fix` replaces it with a
  real ID.

<a id="term-PLEML"></a>

PLEML
: The SysML v2 library for product-line modelling from MBSE4U, the successor of VAMOS.

<a id="term-role"></a>

role
: A set of west groups that decides which repos a workspace checks out, for example `ee`
  or `integration`.

<a id="term-stub"></a>

stub
: A generated, read-only SysML element (`concern` or `requirement`) that stands for a
  need, so the model can refer to it.

<a id="term-suspect-link"></a>

suspect link
: A link whose target changed after the link was last confirmed.

<a id="term-SYSMOD"></a>

SYSMOD
: The systems engineering method by Tim Weilkiens that XDMOD follows.

<a id="term-tombstone"></a>

tombstone
: A record that curatrix keeps for a generated need whose source was deleted without
  retiring it first. It lasts until the next baseline.

<a id="term-trace-link"></a>

trace link
: A typed link from one need to another, written on the more concrete side.

<a id="term-VAMOS"></a>

VAMOS
: The variant method by Tim Weilkiens. XDMOD uses it through PLEML.

<a id="term-view"></a>

view
: A diagram of part of the SysML model, defined in the model and rendered by curatrix as an
  editable `.drawio.svg`.

<a id="term-west"></a>

west
: Zephyr’s tool for managing several git repos as one workspace.

<a id="term-worktree-set"></a>

worktree set
: A folder `.worktrees/<branch>/` with git worktrees of the repos, so an agent can work on
  a branch without touching the main checkouts.

<a id="term-zdocs"></a>

zdocs
: The documentation engine that builds and links the documents of all repos.


# reference/id-scheme.html.md

<a id="ref-id-scheme"></a>

# ID scheme

Every need has an ID. IDs are stable, never reused, readable, and unique across the whole
workspace. They work in every tool: sphinx-needs, SysML short names, KiCad fields, FreeCAD
properties, Doxygen tags and test reports. The scheme is new; it does not reuse older ID schemes
([*A new ID prefix scheme (XD-ADR-0013)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0013)).

## Format

```text
<DOMAIN>-<KIND>-<NNNN>   e.g.  SYS-REQ-0012, SW-TC-0103, EE-CMP-0007, INT-ITC-0003
TR-<TESTCASE-ID>-<RUN>   e.g.  TR-SW-TC-0103-3f9a1c2e   (test results only)
```

- `DOMAIN`: `SYS`, `SW`, `EE`, `ME`, `INT` (integration and system verification),
  `XD` for the framework’s own items and `PRJ` for project-level items ([*ID format DOMAIN-KIND-NNNN (XD-ADR-0071)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0071),
  [*Decisions become sphinx-needs (XD-ADR-0109)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0109)).
- `KIND`: 2 to 5 capital letters. Domain and kind together name the need type.
- `NNNN`: a number with 4 digits, zero-padded, issued per kind. Above 9999 it simply grows.
- `RUN`: the first 8 hex digits of the run record’s hash (HIL runs) or of the JUnit file. So a
  test result is unique per run.
- A usage of a definition may get `<ID>.<n>` ([*The definition holds the tr... (XD-ADR-0117)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0117)).
- Regex:
  `^((SYS|SW|EE|ME|INT|XD|PRJ)-[A-Z]{2,5}-[0-9]{4,}|TR-(SYS|SW|EE|ME|INT)-[A-Z]{2,5}-[0-9]{4,}-[0-9a-f]{8})$`

**No project code in the sources** ([*No project code in the sources (XD-ADR-0072)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0072)). All repos of a project share one ID space.
Where IDs leave the workspace (bundles, published `needs.json`, shared affirmatrix cases), the
exporting tool puts a project code in front, with `:` as the separator. Example (robot arm):
`RA:SYS-REQ-0012`.

## Kinds

Generated from curatrix and the needs configuration:

| Kind       | Need type                  | Directive   |
|------------|----------------------------|-------------|
| `EE-CMP`   | Circuit Block / Component  | `ee-cmp`    |
| `EE-PCBA`  | PCBA                       | `ee-pcba`   |
| `EE-REQ`   | EE Requirement             | `ee-req`    |
| `EE-TC`    | EE Test Case               | `ee-tc`     |
| `INT-ITC`  | Integration Test Case      | `int-itc`   |
| `INT-STC`  | System Test Case           | `int-stc`   |
| `ME-ASM`   | Assembly                   | `me-asm`    |
| `ME-PART`  | Part                       | `me-part`   |
| `ME-REQ`   | ME Requirement             | `me-req`    |
| `ME-TC`    | ME Test Case               | `me-tc`     |
| `PRJ-DEC`  | Project Decision           | `prj-dec`   |
| `SW-ARCH`  | SW Architecture Element    | `sw-arch`   |
| `SW-DD`    | SW Detailed Design Element | `sw-dd`     |
| `SW-IMPL`  | Code Unit                  | `sw-impl`   |
| `SW-REQ`   | SW Requirement             | `sw-req`    |
| `SW-TC`    | SW Test Case               | `sw-tc`     |
| `SYS-CFG`  | Configuration              | `sys-cfg`   |
| `SYS-EL`   | System Model Element       | `sys-el`    |
| `SYS-FEAT` | Feature                    | `sys-feat`  |
| `SYS-IF`   | Interface                  | `sys-if`    |
| `SYS-NEED` | Stakeholder Need           | `sys-need`  |
| `SYS-REQ`  | System Requirement         | `sys-req`   |
| `SYS-STH`  | Stakeholder                | `sys-sth`   |
| `SYS-UC`   | Use Case                   | `sys-uc`    |
| `SYS-VIEW` | (reserved, not a need)     |             |
| `XD-ADR`   | Framework Decision         | `xd-adr`    |
| `XD-CHECK` | curatrix Check             | `xd-check`  |
| `XD-RULE`  | Method Rule                | `xd-rule`   |

`SYS-VIEW` is a reserved kind that is not a need. It is only used as the SysML short name of a
view ([*View definitions live in th... (XD-ADR-0085)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0085)). Its numbers still come from the ledger. Configurations and features have the
kinds `SYS-CFG` and `SYS-FEAT` ([*IDs for configurations and ... (XD-ADR-0097)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0097)). SW test case IDs come from the ledger and a tool
writes them into the ZTEST comment ([*SW test case IDs come from ... (XD-ADR-0073)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0073)).

## Where the ID lives in each tool

| Tool               | Where the ID is written                                                                                                                                                                       | Read by                          |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| sphinx-needs (rst) | `:id:` of the directive                                                                                                                                                                       | Sphinx                           |
| SysML v2           | short name: `part def <'SYS-EL-0012'> ArmController { … }`; stubs use the<br/>requirement’s ID                                                                                                | Pilot JSON, then curatrix        |
| KiCad              | hidden symbol or sheet field `TraceID`; links in further hidden fields (`Realizes`,<br/>`Satisfies`, `Conforms`, `PartOf`)                                                                    | curatrix (plain Python)          |
| FreeCAD            | object properties `TraceID`, `Realizes`, `Satisfies`, `Conforms`, `PartOf`                                                                                                                    | `Document.xml`, read by curatrix |
| Doxygen / C        | `@xdid{SW-IMPL-0004}`, `\satisfies`, `\verifies`; test IDs in the ZTEST comment                                                                                                               | Doxygen XML, then zdocs          |
| Twister / JUnit    | the test case’s `SW-TC` ID in the test name or a property                                                                                                                                     | test reports, then `TR` needs    |
| Devicetree         | `trace-id` property of the project’s own binding, never on upstream nodes<br/>([*Small corrections from rese... (XD-ADR-0057)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0057) (f)) | the devicetree check             |

## The ledger

Each repo keeps one ledger file, `ids.yaml`. It lists **every number ever issued** per kind
that the repo owns, one per line. It is append-only. Listing every number (not just the last)
means that two PRs that issue the same number touch the same line, so git reports a conflict
([*ID collisions show up as gi... (XD-ADR-0122)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0122)).

```yaml
# Every number issued per kind, one per line. Append-only.
SYS-REQ:
  - 41
  - 42
SYS-NEED:
  - 17
SYS-FEAT: []       # owned, nothing issued yet
```

A kind with nothing issued yet is written `KIND: []`. That line makes the repo the owner of
the kind.

## Issuing IDs

- **Placeholders.** Write a need with a placeholder ID of the form `<KIND>-NEW-<tag>`, for
  example the kind `SYS-REQ` followed by `-NEW-a`. Then run
  `curatrix ids fix <repo>`. It replaces every placeholder with the next free number
  (`max(ledger, IDs in the sources) + 1`) and adds it to the ledger. The same placeholder gets
  the same ID in every file.
- `curatrix ids new <KIND> [FILE]` issues one ID, and with `FILE` replaces that file’s first
  placeholder of the kind.
- Never invent a number. Never reuse one.
- **Parallel PRs.** Two PRs may issue the same number. The second to rebase gets a ledger
  conflict. Rerun `curatrix ids fix`, which renumbers that PR’s new IDs. Rulesets require PRs
  to be up to date with `main` before merge, so the duplicate check runs on the combined state.
- **Retiring.** A retired need keeps its ID with `status: retired` ([*Small corrections from rese... (XD-ADR-0057)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0057) (e),
  [*Retiring generated needs (XD-ADR-0119)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0119)). When it is finally deleted, the ledger still holds its number.

## Rules

<a id="needtable-reference/id-scheme-0"></a>

| ID                                                                       | Title                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| [XD-RULE-0015](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0015) | An ID matches the scheme and its need type     |
| [XD-RULE-0016](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0016) | IDs are unique                                 |
| [XD-RULE-0017](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0017) | No placeholders on main                        |
| [XD-RULE-0018](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0018) | The ledger is never behind the sources         |
| [XD-RULE-0019](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0019) | Test report IDs are mapped to TR IDs           |
| [XD-RULE-0020](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0020) | IDs are never reused; retire before you delete |
- [*An ID matches the scheme an... (XD-RULE-0015)*](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0015) is checked by [*IDs match the scheme and th... (XD-CHECK-0003)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0003).
- [*IDs are unique (XD-RULE-0016)*](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0016) is checked by [*no duplicate IDs across doc... (XD-CHECK-0010)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0010) across documents and in the full set.
- [*No placeholders on main (XD-RULE-0017)*](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0017) is checked by [*no placeholder IDs (XD-CHECK-0013)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0013).
- [*The ledger is never behind ... (XD-RULE-0018)*](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0018) is checked by [*IDs in the sources are in t... (XD-CHECK-0014)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0014).
- [*IDs are never reused; retir... (XD-RULE-0020)*](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0020) is helped by [*tombstones of deleted gener... (XD-CHECK-0012)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0012) (tombstones of deleted generated needs).
- [*Test report IDs are mapped ... (XD-RULE-0019)*](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0019) is applied by the test-report extractor.

# reference/repo-layouts.html.md

<a id="ref-repo-layouts"></a>

# Repo layouts

Every repo that uses XDMOD follows one common pattern. Domain repos add their own folders.
Examples are from the robot arm.

## Common pattern

```text
<repo>/
  README.md
  checks.yaml            what `curatrix check` runs for this repo
  ids.yaml               ID ledger
  requirements.txt       pinned pip packages this repo needs
  tools.yaml             pinned non-pip tools (name, version, source, sha256)
  docs/
    documents.yaml       zdocs registry: own documents and upstream documents
    CMakeLists.txt
    <doc-id>/            one folder per document (conf.py and rst)
  generated/             committed generated files, checked by `curatrix check`
  claude/                agent material for this repo
  .github/
    workflows/           thin callers of the reusable workflows in xdmod
    pull_request_template.md
  .gitattributes         diff drivers (e.g. *.FCStd diff=fcstd -merge)
```

Rules:

- **No build output in repos** ([*Build output only under build/ (XD-RULE-0040)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0040), [*no build output inside the ... (XD-CHECK-0026)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0026)). Everything goes to
  `<workspace>/build/<area>/` ([*Every check also runs locally (XD-ADR-0040)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0040)). `<area>` is the repo name, `full` for the full
  set, the branch for worktree builds ([*Parallel agents work in git... (XD-ADR-0114)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0114)), or a named step.
- **Generated files are committed only in** `generated/`, except where the tool needs them next
  to the source: SysML stubs in `model/generated/` and views in `views/`.
- **Folder names are lowercase with dashes.** Each PCBA, assembly and configuration gets its own
  folder, so adding one never moves another.

## Systems engineering repo

```text
model/                  *.sysml per SYSMOD step (see the SYSMOD mapping)
model/generated/        stubs from the needs
views/                  <view>.drawio.svg
generated/              model.json, model-needs.json
docs/se-req/  docs/se-arch/
```

## EE repo

```text
pcba/<name>/            one KiCad project per PCBA, with project-local library tables
proto/<config>/         prototype wiring per prototype configuration (KiCad or WireViz)
lib/                    project-local symbols, footprints, 3D models
tests/                  scripted EE checks (netlist vs. pin map, ERC), JUnit output
generated/              cad-needs.json
docs/                   EE requirements and design; one document per PCBA and per
                        prototype configuration
```

KiCad library tables refer to the shared libraries only through variables (`${XD_KICAD_SYMBOLS}`
and so on) and to `lib/` through `${KIPRJMOD}`. `curatrix launch kicad` sets the variables
([*Pinned, isolated component ... (XD-ADR-0080)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0080)). There is one document per PCBA and one per prototype configuration ([*One EE document per PCBA an... (XD-ADR-0102)*](explanation/decisions/documents.html.md#XD-ADR-0102)).

## ME repo

```text
parts/<part>.FCStd      single parts, stored uncompressed
assemblies/<asm>/       <asm>.FCStd and assembly-specific parts
lib/                    project-local parts
templates/              TechDraw templates
print/                  print-settings profiles
tests/                  scripted ME checks, JUnit output
generated/              cad-needs.json, semantic JSON of each .FCStd
docs/
```

FreeCAD files are stored uncompressed, with a git textconv for readable diffs ([*FreeCAD files uncompressed,... (XD-ADR-0056)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0056),
[*Design files are stored unc... (XD-RULE-0039)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0039)).

## SW repo

```text
app/                    the firmware application
dts/bindings/           the project's own devicetree bindings, with trace-id
tests/<suite>/          unit and hardware test suites, with test IDs from the ledger
docs/                   SW requirements, architecture and design, API (Doxygen),
                        test spec, test report
```

SW architecture is written in rst in iteration 1 ([*SW architecture in rst in i... (XD-ADR-0069)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0069)). Test reports are separate
documents from the test specs ([*Test reports are separate d... (XD-ADR-0099)*](explanation/decisions/documents.html.md#XD-ADR-0099)).

## Integration repo

```text
tests/                  system and integration test cases
hil/<setup>/            HIL setups: hardware map, fixtures, runner config
docs/                   system and integration test spec and report
branch `evidence`       orphan branch with HIL run records, never merged
```

Every test that verifies a system requirement or interface lives here ([*Tests live by what they verify (XD-ADR-0104)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0104)).

## Manifest repo

```text
west.yml                imports submanifests/
submanifests/*.yml
scripts/bootstrap.sh    first-time setup; a copy of xdmod/templates/bootstrap.sh
docs/                   full-set registry and the project overview document
.github/workflows/      bump bot, full-set build, Pages publishing
```

`scripts/bootstrap.sh` is a copy of the xdmod template ([*bootstrap.sh is a copy of t... (XD-ADR-0107)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0107)); [*scripts/bootstrap.sh matche... (XD-CHECK-0029)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0029) warns when
it drifts ([*Template copies match the t... (XD-RULE-0043)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0043)).

## xdmod

```text
claude/                 planning folder and shared agent material: skills, commands, checklists
launch/CLAUDE.md        launch file, copied to the workspace root by the bootstrap
curatrix/               the tool (Python package)
sphinx/                 Sphinx extensions and the shared conf helper
needs/                  needs_config.toml (need types, link types, schema rules)
sysml/                  SysML library: trace metadata, @XdView
templates/              bootstrap.sh and other templates
workflows/              reusable GitHub workflows
docs/xdmod-manual/  docs/xdmod-ref/
```

## Agent material

| Where                                              | What                                                                          | Shared or local   |
|----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| `xdmod/launch/CLAUDE.md` → `<workspace>/CLAUDE.md` | workspace rules: run from the root, limits, build paths, trace rule, trailers | shared            |
| `xdmod/claude/skills/`                             | skills per SYSMOD step, EARS writing, ID issuing, change workflow             | shared            |
| `xdmod/claude/commands/`                           | slash commands, e.g. `/review-pr`                                             | shared            |
| `<repo>/claude/CLAUDE.md`                          | repo rules: layout, checks, pitfalls                                          | local             |
| `<repo>/claude/skills/`, `commands/`               | domain skills, e.g. KiCad edits through scripts                               | local             |

The bootstrap links all skills and commands into `<workspace>/.claude/`, prefixed with the
repo name ([*The bootstrap assembles .cl... (XD-ADR-0103)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0103)).


# reference/sysmod-mapping.html.md

<a id="ref-sysmod-mapping"></a>

# SYSMOD mapping

How each SYSMOD step maps to a work product, where it is authored, its need type, and the
document it appears in. Background: [SYSMOD and SysML v2](explanation/sysmod-and-sysml.html.md).

## Steps and work products

| #   | SYSMOD step / work product                                                                                                                           | Authored in                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Need type (ID kind)                    | Document                                                                                                                                                    |
|-----|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 01  | Project (owner, purpose, process)                                                                                                                    | `.sysml` (`#project`), short                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | —                                      | requirements spec, introduction                                                                                                                             |
| 02  | Brownfield architecture                                                                                                                              | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | —                                      | skipped for greenfield projects                                                                                                                             |
| 03  | Problem statement                                                                                                                                    | rst, one need with `category: problem`; `concern` stub generated ([*The problem statement is a ... (XD-ADR-0074)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0074))                                                                                                        | `SYS-NEED`                             | requirements spec                                                                                                                                           |
| 04  | Stakeholders                                                                                                                                         | rst, with SYSMOD’s fields (categories, risk, effort); `part` stubs generated                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `SYS-STH`                              | requirements spec                                                                                                                                           |
| 05  | Stakeholder needs                                                                                                                                    | rst; `concern` stubs generated                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `SYS-NEED`                             | requirements spec                                                                                                                                           |
| 06  | System idea and system objectives                                                                                                                    | idea: `.sysml` (`systemIdeaContext`); objectives: rst, needs with<br/>`category: objective` ([*System objectives are stake... (XD-ADR-0075)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0075))                                                                             | `SYS-NEED`                             | requirements spec                                                                                                                                           |
| 07  | System context (actors, system ports, interfaces)                                                                                                    | `.sysml` (`specificationContext`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `SYS-EL` (`layer: context`), `SYS-IF`  | system architecture                                                                                                                                         |
| 08  | Use cases (and flows)                                                                                                                                | `.sysml` (`use case … : SystemUseCase`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `SYS-UC`                               | requirements spec                                                                                                                                           |
| 09  | System requirements                                                                                                                                  | rst, EARS ([*EARS for system and domain ... (XD-ADR-0039)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0039)), with value fields ([*Requirement values are need... (XD-ADR-0076)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0076)); `requirement` stubs generated | `SYS-REQ`                              | requirements spec                                                                                                                                           |
| 10a | Functional architecture                                                                                                                              | `.sysml` (`functionalContext`) ([*A short functional architec... (XD-ADR-0078)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0078))                                                                                                                                          | `SYS-EL` (`layer: functional`)         | system architecture                                                                                                                                         |
| 10b | Logical architecture                                                                                                                                 | `.sysml` (`logicalContext`), `allocate` functional to logical                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `SYS-EL` (`layer: logical`)            | system architecture                                                                                                                                         |
| 10c | Product architecture (150 %, with variation points) and allocation                                                                                   | `.sysml` (`productContext`), `allocate` logical to product                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `SYS-EL` (`layer: product`, `configs`) | system architecture                                                                                                                                         |
| 10d | Features and configurations (VAMOS/PLEML, [*Variants follow VAMOS throu... (XD-ADR-0092)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0092)) | `.sysml`: feature model, one product model per configuration                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `SYS-FEAT`, `SYS-CFG`                  | system architecture; one page per configuration ([*One variant-aware document set (XD-ADR-0096)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0096)) |
| 11  | Verification and validation                                                                                                                          | rst test specs in the integration repo ([*An integration repo for sys... (XD-ADR-0066)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0066)); a SysML verification context later                                                                                              | `INT-STC`, `INT-ITC`                   | system and integration test spec                                                                                                                            |

Links between the products follow the link table in [Trace model](reference/trace-model.html.md), for example:

- `SYS-REQ` refines `SYS-NEED` (SYSMOD’s `frame`, kept in sphinx-needs).
- `SYS-UC` addresses `SYS-NEED`.
- A product `SYS-EL` satisfies `SYS-REQ` (SysML `satisfy` on the stub) and realizes a
  logical `SYS-EL` (from `allocate`).

## Files in the systems engineering repo

```text
model/                  SysML sources (authored)
  project.sysml         01
  context.sysml         06, 07: idea and specification context, actors, ports, interfaces
  usecases.sysml        08
  functional.sysml      10a
  logical.sysml         10b
  product.sysml         10c: product context and allocations
  features.sysml        10d: feature model (PLEML)
  configs.sysml         10d: configurations, one product model each
  views.sysml           view definitions
  generated/            stubs from the needs (committed, checked)
docs/
  se-req/               requirements spec: 01, 03, 04, 05, 06, 08 (generated), 09
  se-arch/              system architecture: 07, 10 (from the model) and views
generated/              model.json, model-needs.json (committed, checked)
views/                  <view>.drawio.svg (committed, checked)
```

## Requirement fields

| Field                                       | Example                                                           | Use                                                                                                                                                                           |
|---------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `ears`                                      | `ubiquitous`, `event`, `state`, `optional`, `unwanted`, `complex` | the EARS pattern, checked against the sentence ([*EARS pattern matches the se... (XD-CHECK-0022)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0022))                |
| `quantity`, `unit`, `min`, `max`, `nominal` | `latency`, `ms`, —, `50`, —                                       | values that model attributes and tests can be checked against ([*requirement values agree wi... (XD-CHECK-0021)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0021)) |
| `verification_method`                       | `test`                                                            | test, analysis, inspection or demonstration                                                                                                                                   |
| `category`                                  | `functional`, `performance`, `interface`, `constraint`            | grouping in the spec                                                                                                                                                          |


# reference/trace-model.html.md

<a id="ref-trace-model"></a>

# Trace model

The trace model names every need type, every link type and every shared field. One shared file,
`xdmod/needs/needs_config.toml`, defines them for every document of every repo ([*One shared needs configuration (XD-RULE-0007)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0007)).
The tables on this page are generated from that file. The reasons behind the model are in
[The V-model and trace links](explanation/v-model-and-traces.html.md).

## Need types

Each need type has a directive name equal to its ID kind in lower case (`.. sys-req::` for
`SYS-REQ-0012`). A link type is declared only on the need type that holds it ([*Link types are declared on ... (XD-RULE-0002)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0002)).

| Directive   | ID prefix   | Need type                  | Link types (→ targets)                                                                       |
|-------------|-------------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `sys-sth`   | `SYS-STH-`  | Stakeholder                |                                                                                              |
| `sys-need`  | `SYS-NEED-` | Stakeholder Need           | `raised_by` → `sys-sth`; `addresses` → `sys-need`                                            |
| `sys-uc`    | `SYS-UC-`   | Use Case                   | `addresses` → `sys-need` (min 1)                                                             |
| `sys-req`   | `SYS-REQ-`  | System Requirement         | `refines` → `sys-need` (min 1)                                                               |
| `sys-if`    | `SYS-IF-`   | Interface                  |                                                                                              |
| `sys-el`    | `SYS-EL-`   | System Model Element       | `satisfies` → `sys-req`; `realizes` → `sys-uc`, `sys-el`                                     |
| `sys-cfg`   | `SYS-CFG-`  | Configuration              | `configures` → `sys-el` (min 1)                                                              |
| `sys-feat`  | `SYS-FEAT-` | Feature                    |                                                                                              |
| `int-stc`   | `INT-STC-`  | System Test Case           | `verifies` → `sys-req` (min 1)                                                               |
| `int-itc`   | `INT-ITC-`  | Integration Test Case      | `verifies` → `sys-req`, `sys-if` (min 1)                                                     |
| `sw-req`    | `SW-REQ-`   | SW Requirement             | `refines` → `sys-req`, `sys-if`                                                              |
| `sw-arch`   | `SW-ARCH-`  | SW Architecture Element    | `realizes` → `sys-el`; `satisfies` → `sw-req`; `conforms` → `sys-if`                         |
| `sw-dd`     | `SW-DD-`    | SW Detailed Design Element | `refines` → `sw-arch` (min 1); `satisfies` → `sw-req`; `conforms` → `sys-if`                 |
| `sw-impl`   | `SW-IMPL-`  | Code Unit                  | `implements` → `sw-dd`, `sw-arch` (min 1); `satisfies` → `sw-req`                            |
| `sw-tc`     | `SW-TC-`    | SW Test Case               | `verifies` → `sw-req`, `sw-dd` (min 1)                                                       |
| `ee-req`    | `EE-REQ-`   | EE Requirement             | `refines` → `sys-req`, `sys-if`                                                              |
| `ee-pcba`   | `EE-PCBA-`  | PCBA                       | `realizes` → `sys-el`; `satisfies` → `ee-req`; `conforms` → `sys-if`                         |
| `ee-cmp`    | `EE-CMP-`   | Circuit Block / Component  | `realizes` → `sys-el`; `satisfies` → `ee-req`; `conforms` → `sys-if`; `part_of` → `ee-pcba`  |
| `ee-tc`     | `EE-TC-`    | EE Test Case               | `verifies` → `ee-req` (min 1)                                                                |
| `me-req`    | `ME-REQ-`   | ME Requirement             | `refines` → `sys-req`, `sys-if`                                                              |
| `me-asm`    | `ME-ASM-`   | Assembly                   | `realizes` → `sys-el`; `satisfies` → `me-req`; `conforms` → `sys-if`                         |
| `me-part`   | `ME-PART-`  | Part                       | `realizes` → `sys-el`; `satisfies` → `me-req`; `conforms` → `sys-if`; `part_of` → `me-asm`   |
| `me-tc`     | `ME-TC-`    | ME Test Case               | `verifies` → `me-req` (min 1)                                                                |
| `xd-adr`    | `XD-ADR-`   | Framework Decision         | `refines` → `xd-adr`; `revises` → `xd-adr`; `supersedes` → `xd-adr`                          |
| `xd-rule`   | `XD-RULE-`  | Method Rule                | `decided_by` → `xd-adr` (min 1)                                                              |
| `xd-check`  | `XD-CHECK-` | curatrix Check             | `enforces` → `xd-rule` (min 1)                                                               |
| `prj-dec`   | `PRJ-DEC-`  | Project Decision           | `follows` → `xd-adr`; `refines` → `prj-dec`; `revises` → `prj-dec`; `supersedes` → `prj-dec` |
| `tr`        | `TR-`       | Test Result                | `result_of` → `int-stc`, `int-itc`, `sw-tc`, `ee-tc`, `me-tc` (min 1)                        |
| `testfile`  | `TF_`       | Test-File                  |                                                                                              |
| `testsuite` | `TS_`       | Test-Suite                 |                                                                                              |
| `testcase`  | `TC_`       | Test-Case                  | `result_of` → `int-stc`, `int-itc`, `sw-tc`, `ee-tc`, `me-tc`                                |

## Where the need types live

| Area                  | Kinds                                               | Authored or generated                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Systems engineering   | `SYS-STH`, `SYS-NEED`, `SYS-REQ`                    | authored in rst; stakeholder needs and requirements get SysML stubs ([*Read-only requirement stubs... (XD-ADR-0036)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0036))                                               |
|                       | `SYS-UC`, `SYS-IF`, `SYS-EL`, `SYS-CFG`, `SYS-FEAT` | authored in SysML, generated as needs by the model extractor                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Integration           | `INT-STC`, `INT-ITC`                                | authored in rst                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Software              | `SW-REQ`, `SW-ARCH`, `SW-DD`                        | authored in rst (`SW-DD` also as a Doxygen group)                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                       | `SW-IMPL`, `SW-TC`                                  | generated from Doxygen tags and ZTEST annotations                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Electrical            | `EE-REQ`, `EE-TC`                                   | authored in rst (test cases also from scripted checks)                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                       | `EE-PCBA`, `EE-CMP`                                 | generated from KiCad project and symbol or sheet fields ([*Trace IDs live inside the C... (XD-ADR-0023)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0023))                                                           |
| Mechanical            | `ME-REQ`, `ME-TC`                                   | authored in rst                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                       | `ME-ASM`, `ME-PART`                                 | generated from FreeCAD object properties                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Framework and project | `XD-ADR`, `XD-RULE`, `PRJ-DEC`                      | authored in rst ([*Decisions become sphinx-needs (XD-ADR-0109)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0109), [*Method rules are needs (XD-ADR-0110)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0110)) |
|                       | `XD-CHECK`                                          | generated from curatrix’s check catalogue                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Results               | `TR`                                                | generated from test output; for HIL runs from the evidence branch                                                                                                                                                             |

Prototype wiring is EE content: a KiCad schematic of the prototype, whose elements are
`EE-CMP` with `configs` set to the prototype configuration ([*Prototype wiring is EE content (XD-ADR-0067)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0067)). Code units must
`implements` a design element and may also `satisfies` a SW requirement directly
([*Code units implement design... (XD-ADR-0070)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0070)).

## Definitions and instances

- **The definition holds the ID** ([*The definition holds the tr... (XD-ADR-0117)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0117)): a SysML `part def`, a KiCad sheet file, a
  FreeCAD part file. Its usages are listed in an `instances` field, not as separate needs.
- A usage gets its own ID `<ID>.<n>` (for example `SYS-EL-0012.1`) only if it has its own
  requirement.
- **Only model elements with trace links become needs** ([*Only linked model elements ... (XD-ADR-0118)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0118)): `satisfy`,
  `allocate`, or a link from another repo.

## Link types

The owner is the need type that holds the link. “Min” is the number of targets the schema
requires. Some minimums depend on a field and are schema rules instead:

- A domain requirement without an upstream link must have `derived: true` and a
  `rationale`.
- `raised_by` is required for stakeholder needs with `category: need` or `objective`.
- Every domain design element needs at least one `realizes` or `satisfies` ([*No orphan design elements (XD-RULE-0010)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0010)).
- Coverage minimums are graph rules ([*Every system requirement is... (XD-RULE-0008)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0008), [*Every requirement is verified (XD-RULE-0009)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0009)), not single-need rules.

| Link         | Owner (source)   | Targets                                         |   Min | Meaning                                                                                       |
|--------------|------------------|-------------------------------------------------|-------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `raised_by`  | `sys-need`       | `sys-sth`                                       |     0 | The stakeholder who raised the need (min 1 for category need/objective).                      |
| `addresses`  | `sys-need`       | `sys-need`                                      |     0 | A need or objective addresses the problem statement (D81).                                    |
| `addresses`  | `sys-uc`         | `sys-need`                                      |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `refines`    | `sys-req`        | `sys-need`                                      |     1 | The requirement answers this need (SYSMOD frame).                                             |
| `satisfies`  | `sys-el`         | `sys-req`                                       |     0 | The model element satisfies the requirement (SysML satisfy).                                  |
| `realizes`   | `sys-el`         | `sys-uc`, `sys-el`                              |     0 | functional -> use case; logical -> functional; product -> logical (D85, D102).                |
| `configures` | `sys-cfg`        | `sys-el`                                        |     1 | The configuration is one product of the 150 % architecture.                                   |
| `verifies`   | `int-stc`        | `sys-req`                                       |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `verifies`   | `int-itc`        | `sys-req`, `sys-if`                             |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `refines`    | `sw-req`         | `sys-req`, `sys-if`                             |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `realizes`   | `sw-arch`        | `sys-el`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `satisfies`  | `sw-arch`        | `sw-req`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `conforms`   | `sw-arch`        | `sys-if`                                        |     0 | The element meets a peer interface (pin map, connector, mounting).                            |
| `refines`    | `sw-dd`          | `sw-arch`                                       |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `satisfies`  | `sw-dd`          | `sw-req`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `conforms`   | `sw-dd`          | `sys-if`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `implements` | `sw-impl`        | `sw-dd`, `sw-arch`                              |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `satisfies`  | `sw-impl`        | `sw-req`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `verifies`   | `sw-tc`          | `sw-req`, `sw-dd`                               |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `refines`    | `ee-req`         | `sys-req`, `sys-if`                             |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `realizes`   | `ee-pcba`        | `sys-el`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `satisfies`  | `ee-pcba`        | `ee-req`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `conforms`   | `ee-pcba`        | `sys-if`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `realizes`   | `ee-cmp`         | `sys-el`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `satisfies`  | `ee-cmp`         | `ee-req`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `conforms`   | `ee-cmp`         | `sys-if`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `part_of`    | `ee-cmp`         | `ee-pcba`                                       |     0 | Structure of the domain design.                                                               |
| `verifies`   | `ee-tc`          | `ee-req`                                        |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `refines`    | `me-req`         | `sys-req`, `sys-if`                             |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `realizes`   | `me-asm`         | `sys-el`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `satisfies`  | `me-asm`         | `me-req`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `conforms`   | `me-asm`         | `sys-if`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `realizes`   | `me-part`        | `sys-el`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
