| `satisfies`  | `me-part`        | `me-req`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `conforms`   | `me-part`        | `sys-if`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `part_of`    | `me-part`        | `me-asm`                                        |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `verifies`   | `me-tc`          | `me-req`                                        |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `refines`    | `xd-adr`         | `xd-adr`                                        |     0 | The newer decision adds detail to an older one, which stays in force.                         |
| `revises`    | `xd-adr`         | `xd-adr`                                        |     0 | The newer decision changes part of an older one (the older one gets decision_status revised). |
| `supersedes` | `xd-adr`         | `xd-adr`                                        |     0 | The newer decision replaces an older one completely (decision_status superseded).             |
| `decided_by` | `xd-rule`        | `xd-adr`                                        |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `enforces`   | `xd-check`       | `xd-rule`                                       |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `follows`    | `prj-dec`        | `xd-adr`                                        |     0 | The project decision applies or tailors a framework decision.                                 |
| `refines`    | `prj-dec`        | `prj-dec`                                       |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `revises`    | `prj-dec`        | `prj-dec`                                       |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `supersedes` | `prj-dec`        | `prj-dec`                                       |     0 |                                                                                               |
| `result_of`  | `tr`             | `int-stc`, `int-itc`, `sw-tc`, `ee-tc`, `me-tc` |     1 |                                                                                               |
| `result_of`  | `testcase`       | `int-stc`, `int-itc`, `sw-tc`, `ee-tc`, `me-tc` |     0 |                                                                                               |

## Fields

| Field                 | Values                                                                                 | Meaning                                                                                                                                                    |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `status`              | `draft`, `valid`, `retired`                                                            | draft | valid | retired (D64e, D130). draft: structure checks only, no coverage.                                                                           |
| `source_file`         | string                                                                                 | Generated needs: source path relative to the repo.                                                                                                         |
| `legacy_id`           | string                                                                                 | The old name of a decision or rule before it became a need, e.g. D37 or R3 (D120).                                                                         |
| `date`                | string matching `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$`                                         | XD-ADR / PRJ-DEC: the day the decision was made (YYYY-MM-DD).                                                                                              |
| `decision_status`     | `accepted`, `revised`, `superseded`                                                    | XD-ADR / PRJ-DEC: accepted | revised (a newer decision changed part of it) | superseded (a newer decision replaced it). The newer decision holds the link. |
| `check_id`            | string matching `^CK-[A-Z][0-9]+$`                                                     | XD-CHECK: the check’s ID in curatrix (CK-…), as used by \`curatrix check –only\`.                                                                          |
| `instances`           | list of string                                                                         | Usages of a definition need (D128), e.g. leader.joint1.                                                                                                    |
| `configs`             | list of string matching `^SYS-CFG-[0-9]{4,}$`                                          | SYS-CFG IDs the element belongs to; empty = all (D103).                                                                                                    |
| `qualified_name`      | string                                                                                 | SysML qualified name of the element (generated needs).                                                                                                     |
| `sysml_kind`          | string                                                                                 | SysML metaclass of the element (generated needs).                                                                                                          |
| `category`            | `problem`, `objective`, `need`, `functional`, `performance`, `interface`, `constraint` | SYS-NEED: problem | objective | need. Requirements: functional | performance | interface | constraint.                                                     |
| `ears`                | `ubiquitous`, `event`, `state`, `optional`, `unwanted`, `complex`                      | EARS pattern of the sentence (D12, D45).                                                                                                                   |
| `quantity`            | string                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `unit`                | string                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `min`                 | number                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `max`                 | number                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `nominal`             | number                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `verification_method` | `test`, `analysis`, `inspection`, `demonstration`                                      |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `verification_scope`  | `logical`, `config`                                                                    | logical: evidence from any configuration counts; config: per configuration (D104).                                                                         |
| `where`               | string                                                                                 | Feature condition, e.g. SYS-FEAT-0002 (D103).                                                                                                              |
| `derived`             | boolean                                                                                | Domain requirement without an upstream link (needs a rationale).                                                                                           |
| `rationale`           | string                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `layer`               | `context`, `functional`, `logical`, `product`                                          | SYS-EL only: context | functional | logical | product.                                                                                                     |
| `config`              | string matching `^SYS-CFG-[0-9]{4,}$`                                                  | The single SYS-CFG a test run was made on.                                                                                                                 |
| `method`              | `test`, `hil`, `analysis`, `inspection`, `demonstration`                               | How the evidence was produced (D131).                                                                                                                      |
| `firmware_sha256`     | string matching `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`                                                       |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `shas`                | list of string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+=[0-9a-f]{7,40}$`                             | Pinned repo SHAs of the run: repo=sha entries (R5).                                                                                                        |
| `reviewer`            | string                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `verdict`             | `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, `error`                                                 |                                                                                                                                                            |

Notes on the fields:

- `status`: `draft` needs take part in all structure checks, but don’t count as coverage.
  Generated needs take their status from the source ([*Retiring generated needs (XD-ADR-0119)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0119)): SysML metadata, the KiCad
  field `Status`, the FreeCAD property `Status`, or a Doxygen tag.
- `configs`, `where`, `verification_scope`, `config`: see
  [Variants](explanation/variants.html.md) ([*Variant fields configs, whe... (XD-ADR-0093)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0093), [*Coverage per configuration (XD-ADR-0094)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0094)).
- `ears`, `quantity`, `unit`, `min`, `max`, `nominal`: requirement values
  ([*Requirement values are need... (XD-ADR-0076)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0076)).

## Rules

The trace principles and graph rules:

<a id="needtable-reference/trace-model-0"></a>

| ID                                                                       | Rule            | Title                                                    |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| [XD-RULE-0001](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0001) | trace-model 1.1 | The concrete side holds the link                         |
| [XD-RULE-0002](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0002) | trace-model 1.2 | Link types are declared on the need type that owns them  |
| [XD-RULE-0003](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0003) | trace-model 1.3 | Peer interfaces live in systems engineering              |
| [XD-RULE-0004](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0004) | trace-model 1.4 | Allocation is stored on the concrete side                |
| [XD-RULE-0005](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0005) | trace-model 1.5 | Variants are expressed with configs and where            |
| [XD-RULE-0006](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0006) | trace-model 1.6 | Generated needs follow the same rules                    |
| [XD-RULE-0007](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0007) | trace-model 1.7 | One shared needs configuration                           |
| [XD-RULE-0008](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0008) | R1              | Every system requirement is refined or satisfied         |
| [XD-RULE-0009](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0009) | R2              | Every requirement is verified                            |
| [XD-RULE-0010](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0010) | R3              | No orphan design elements                                |
| [XD-RULE-0011](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0011) | R4              | Links to retired needs are reported, with a grace period |
| [XD-RULE-0012](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0012) | R5              | HIL results carry the firmware hash and the pinned SHAs  |
| [XD-RULE-0013](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0013) | R5a             | Only valid evidence counts                               |
| [XD-RULE-0014](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0014) | R7              | Suspect links are reviewed before a baseline             |

Where each rule is checked:

| Rule                                                                                                        | Checked by                                                                                                                                                                   | Level                                                                                                                                                           |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [*Every system requirement is... (XD-RULE-0008)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0008) | [*every SYS-REQ refined or sa... (XD-CHECK-0006)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0006), full set                                                      | error in the full set                                                                                                                                           |
| [*Every requirement is verified (XD-RULE-0009)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0009)  | [*every requirement verified ... (XD-CHECK-0007)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0007)                                                                | warning in iteration 1, error later ([*Verification coverage is a ... (XD-ADR-0090)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0090))                 |
| [*No orphan design elements (XD-RULE-0010)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0010)      | schema rule and [*no orphans (R3) (XD-CHECK-0004)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0004)                                                               | error                                                                                                                                                           |
| [*Links to retired needs are ... (XD-RULE-0011)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0011) | [*no links to retired needs (... (XD-CHECK-0008)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0008)                                                                | warning on `main` and in PRs; error at the baseline ([*A grace period for retired ... (XD-ADR-0068)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0068)) |
| [*HIL results carry the firmw... (XD-RULE-0012)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0012) | schema rule and [*HIL results carry firmware ... (XD-CHECK-0005)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0005)                                                | error                                                                                                                                                           |
| [*Only valid evidence counts (XD-RULE-0013)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0013)     | [*stale evidence (R5a) (XD-CHECK-0011)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0011)                                                                          | stale results are reported; at the baseline they don’t count                                                                                                    |
| the variant rules                                                                                           | [*variant rules F1, F2, V1-V5 (XD-CHECK-0009)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0009), see [Variant rules](reference/variant-rules.html.md) | error                                                                                                                                                           |
| [*Suspect links are reviewed ... (XD-RULE-0014)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0014) | [*suspect links against the l... (XD-CHECK-0024)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0024) (needs-diff now, affirmatrix later)                            | report in PRs; gate before a baseline                                                                                                                           |

[*Links to retired needs are ... (XD-RULE-0011)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0011) is deliberately not a schema rule: a strict build would turn it into an error at
once, and the grace period would be lost.


# reference/variant-rules.html.md

<a id="ref-variant-rules"></a>

# Variant rules

These rules check a variant model: the feature model, the product models of the configurations,
and the trace links between variant elements ([*Variant rules (XD-ADR-0095)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0095)). All are errors. curatrix checks them
with [*variant rules F1, F2, V1-V5 (XD-CHECK-0009)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0009) (`curatrix variants` runs them alone); the SysML Pilot checks none of them.
They run locally, in PR CI of the systems engineering repo, and in the full set. Background:
[Variants](explanation/variants.html.md).

<a id="needtable-reference/variant-rules-0"></a>

| ID                                                                       | Rule   | Title                                        |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|----------------------------------------------|
| [XD-RULE-0021](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0021) | F1     | A configuration respects its feature tree    |
| [XD-RULE-0022](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0022) | F2     | Feature constraints hold                     |
| [XD-RULE-0023](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0023) | V1     | One product model per configuration          |
| [XD-RULE-0024](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0024) | V2     | Every variation is bound                     |
| [XD-RULE-0025](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0025) | V3     | A variation is bound to its own variant      |
| [XD-RULE-0026](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0026) | V4     | The chosen variant is enabled                |
| [XD-RULE-0027](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0027) | V5     | Exactly one variant per variation            |
| [XD-RULE-0028](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0028) | V6     | Model constraints hold in each product model |
| [XD-RULE-0029](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0029) | T1     | configs matches the source                   |
| [XD-RULE-0030](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0030) | T2     | realizes respects configurations             |
| [XD-RULE-0031](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0031) | T3     | Coverage counts per configuration            |

## Notes

- [*A configuration respects it... (XD-RULE-0021)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0021) and [*Feature constraints hold (XD-RULE-0022)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0022) check the **feature model**: a configuration sets only features of
  its tree, feature groups keep their multiplicity, and every `requires`, `xor` or
  `implies` constraint holds in every configuration.
- [*One product model per confi... (XD-RULE-0023)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0023) to [*Exactly one variant per var... (XD-RULE-0027)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0027) check the **product models**: one product model per configuration,
  every variation bound to one of its own variants, the chosen variant enabled by the
  configuration, and exactly one variant enabled per variation.
- [*The chosen variant is enabled (XD-RULE-0026)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0026): several feature bindings on one element mean **AND**. PLEML does not say this, so
  it is an XDMOD convention.
- [*Model constraints hold in e... (XD-RULE-0028)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0028) checks the `assert constraint` statements of the 150 % model in each product model
  (simple `==`, `implies`, `and`, `or` only).
- [*configs matches the source (XD-RULE-0029)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0029) to [*Coverage counts per configu... (XD-RULE-0031)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0031) check **traces**: `configs` of a generated need equals what the
  source says; a `realizes` link needs the source’s `configs` to be a subset of the target’s;
  a test result counts for a requirement in a configuration only under the coverage rule
  ([*Coverage per configuration (XD-ADR-0094)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0094)).

## What curatrix checks today

Iteration 1 checks [*A configuration respects it... (XD-RULE-0021)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0021), [*Feature constraints hold (XD-RULE-0022)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0022) and [*One product model per confi... (XD-RULE-0023)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0023) to [*Exactly one variant per var... (XD-RULE-0027)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0027) ([*Scope cuts for iteration 1 (XD-ADR-0124)*](explanation/decisions/scope.html.md#XD-ADR-0124)).
[*Model constraints hold in e... (XD-RULE-0028)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0028), [*configs matches the source (XD-RULE-0029)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0029), [*realizes respects configura... (XD-RULE-0030)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0030) and [*Coverage counts per configu... (XD-RULE-0031)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0031) come when the product configuration has real
content.

Example (robot arm): a configuration that chooses both `prototypeBuild` and `productBuild`
breaks [*Feature constraints hold (XD-RULE-0022)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0022) (the two features are `xor`). A product model that binds the variation
`controller` to `customPcba` in the prototype configuration breaks [*The chosen variant is enabled (XD-RULE-0026)*](explanation/rules/variants.html.md#XD-RULE-0026), because
`customPcba` is bound to `productBuild`.


# reference/workspace.html.md

<a id="ref-workspace"></a>

# Workspace

Paths, roles, environment and limits of an XDMOD workspace. Background:
[Many repos, one workspace](explanation/multi-repo.html.md).

## Layout

The workspace root is the west topdir ([*One west topdir at the work... (XD-ADR-0061)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0061)). Every command runs from here
([*All commands run from the w... (XD-ADR-0060)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0060)); paths in output and documents are relative to it.

```text
<workspace>/
  .west/                west config, incl. manifest.group-filter and the role
  .venv/                workspace venv: west, curatrix, pinned packages, opt/ tools
  .xdmod/               workspace-local tool configs, caches, limit overrides (not a repo)
  .claude/              links to the shared and per-repo agent skills and commands
  .worktrees/<branch>/  worktree sets for parallel work
  build/<area>/         all build output
  CLAUDE.md             launch file, copied from xdmod by the bootstrap
  <manifest repo>/
  xdmod/
  <design repos>/       one per domain, plus integration, at the top level
  tools/                zdocs, affirmatrix
  libs/                 SYSMOD library, PLEML, KiCad and FreeCAD libraries
  zephyr/  modules/     Zephyr and its allowlisted modules, if the project uses Zephyr
```

Design repos sit at the top level, because people and agents work in them. Dependencies go
under `tools/` and `libs/` ([*Workspace paths (XD-ADR-0083)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0083)).

## Roles

A role decides which repos a workspace checks out, through west’s group filter
([*West submanifests and proje... (XD-ADR-0079)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0079)). The manifest’s default is minimal ([*A minimal default group filter (XD-ADR-0084)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0084)). The roles that curatrix knows:

| Role          | Group filter (added to the default)   | Gets                                                                                                                                                                  |
|---------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `syseng`      | (manifest default)                    | framework, systems engineering, SYSMOD and PLEML libraries, Zephyr                                                                                                    |
| `ee`          | `+ee`                                 | plus the EE repo and the KiCad libraries without 3D models                                                                                                            |
| `ee3d`        | `+ee,+kicad-3d`                       | like `ee`, plus the KiCad 3D models                                                                                                                                   |
| `me`          | `+me,+freecad-parts`                  | plus the ME repo and the FreeCAD parts library                                                                                                                        |
| `sw`          | `+sw`                                 | plus the SW repo                                                                                                                                                      |
| `integration` | `+ee,+me,+sw,+integration`            | everything except the big libraries ([*The integration role (XD-ADR-0082)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0082))                                 |
| `full`        | all groups                            | everything, for local full builds and baselines                                                                                                                       |
| `ci-full`     | same as `integration`                 | what the full-set CI job uses; CI builds without CAD content ([*CI runs without CAD content (XD-ADR-0049)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0049)) |

Set or change the role with `curatrix bootstrap --role <role>`. Repos that become inactive are
left on disk.

## Bootstrap

From an empty folder (example: the robot arm’s manifest repo):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/tiacsys/robarm-manifest
robarm-manifest/scripts/bootstrap.sh --role ee
```

`bootstrap.sh` creates `.venv` with west, runs `west init -l` and `west update`,
installs curatrix from xdmod (editable), and hands over to `curatrix bootstrap --role <role>`.
That command:

1. sets the role’s group filter and runs `west update`;
2. installs the active repos’ `requirements.txt` into `.venv` and their `tools.yaml`
   tools into `.venv/opt/`, with sha256 checks ([*Tool versions of the refere... (XD-ADR-0014)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0014));
3. copies `xdmod/launch/CLAUDE.md` to the root ([*Agent material in each repo... (XD-ADR-0062)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0062)) and links `.claude/`
   ([*The bootstrap assembles .cl... (XD-ADR-0103)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0103));
4. installs the pre-commit hooks and the FreeCAD diff driver in every active repo
   ([*Pre-commit hooks (XD-ADR-0091)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0091));
5. creates `.xdmod/`;
6. runs `curatrix doctor`.

On branches, use `curatrix update` (it runs `west update -k`). Plain `west update` moves
every project back to its pin, as a detached HEAD.

## Environment

`eval "$(curatrix env)"` sets `PATH` (with `.venv/bin`), `ZEPHYR_BASE`, `JAVA_HOME`,
the `XD_KICAD_*` and `XD_FREECAD_PARTS` library variables, the `env:` entries of the
`tools.yaml` tools, and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. `curatrix run -- <cmd>` runs any
command with this environment and the default limits.

No user-global configuration is used. KiCad, FreeCAD and drawio get workspace-local config
folders under `.xdmod/` through `curatrix launch` ([*Pinned, isolated component ... (XD-ADR-0080)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0080)).

## Limits

Every tool runs under a memory limit and a timeout ([*A memory limit and a timeou... (XD-ADR-0064)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0064), [*Every tool runs under limits (XD-RULE-0044)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0044)). curatrix applies
them itself from `xdmod/curatrix/limits.yaml`, which `<workspace>/.xdmod/limits.yaml` can
override per key. `curatrix limits` shows the resolved table.

- Backend: a systemd user scope with `MemoryMax` and no swap, plus `timeout`. Without a
  systemd user session, curatrix falls back to `timeout` plus `ulimit -v`.
- Exit code 124 means timeout, 137 means killed for memory.
- GUI tools started with `curatrix launch` get a memory limit only, no timeout
  ([*GUI tools get a memory limi... (XD-ADR-0106)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0106)).
- Never raise a limit to make a runaway tool pass; find out why it runs away.

## Commands

`curatrix` is the only command layer ([*One framework tool: curatrix (XD-ADR-0089)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0089), [*The command layer is only c... (XD-ADR-0105)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0105)). The full list of subcommands
and options is in the curatrix reference. The most used:

| Command                                       | Does                                                                                                                                        |
|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `curatrix doctor`                             | checks tools, versions, paths, hooks and the west state                                                                                     |
| `curatrix update`                             | `west update -k`, refresh `.venv`, tools, `.claude/` links and hooks                                                                        |
| `curatrix check <repo> --stage local`         | the repo’s checks ([Checks](reference/checks.html.md))                                                                   |
| `curatrix docs <repo>` / `docs full`          | strict docs build into `build/<area>/docs/`                                                                                                 |
| `curatrix gen <what> <repo>`                  | regenerate the committed generated files                                                                                                    |
| `curatrix ids new <KIND>` / `ids fix <repo>`  | issue IDs, replace placeholders ([ID scheme](reference/id-scheme.html.md))                                                  |
| `curatrix views build|check|normalize <repo>` | views as editable `.drawio.svg`                                                                                                             |
| `curatrix launch kicad|freecad|drawio|claude` | GUI tools with workspace-local config                                                                                                       |
| `curatrix work start|done`                    | worktree sets for parallel work ([*Parallel agents work in git... (XD-ADR-0114)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0114)) |
| `curatrix run -- <cmd>`                       | anything else, with the workspace env and limits                                                                                            |


# tutorials/first-change.html.md

<a id="tut-first-change"></a>

# Your first change

#### NOTE
This tutorial is a skeleton. It is completed in Phase 5 on the real robot-arm repos.

## Goal

You change one requirement and retire another. You see what each check reports, read the change
impact, fix the downstream links, and prepare the affirmation of the suspect links.

## Steps

1. **Start a branch.** Use one branch name in every repo you touch ([*One branch name across repos (XD-ADR-0045)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0045)):
   ```sh
   curatrix work start feat/latency robarm-syseng robarm-ee
   ```

   `curatrix work` is being added (task 4.4c); see [Make a change across repos](howto/cross-repo-change.html.md).
2. **Change a requirement.** Edit the sentence and its value fields together ([*Requirement values agree wi... (XD-RULE-0036)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0036)), e.g.
   `100 ms` becomes `50 ms` and `:max:` becomes `50`. A text change fails no build. Only
   the change impact shows it.
3. **Retire a requirement.** Set `:status: retired`. Never delete a need that others link to
   before it is retired ([*IDs are never reused; retir... (XD-RULE-0020)*](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0020)). Links to it are reported as warnings until the next
   baseline ([*Links to retired needs are ... (XD-RULE-0011)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0011), [*no links to retired needs (... (XD-CHECK-0008)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0008)).
4. **Regenerate** what depends on the needs:
   ```sh
   curatrix docs robarm-syseng
   curatrix gen all robarm-syseng
   ```
5. **Read the change impact.** Compare the needs before and after the change:
   ```sh
   curatrix needs-diff build/main-needs/ build/robarm-syseng/docs/deploy/html/ -o build/robarm-syseng/needs-diff.md
   ```

   It lists changed needs, direct and transitive **suspect** links, and dangling links
   ([*Suspect links are reviewed ... (XD-RULE-0014)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0014)). In a PR, [*needs-diff against the base... (XD-CHECK-0023)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0023) writes the same report.
6. **Fix downstream.** Each downstream owner updates the links that pointed at the retired need,
   on the same branch name, and runs the checks of their repo.
7. **Affirm.** For each suspect link, an agent may prepare a proposal (reason and diff). Only a
   person’s commit affirms it ([*Only a human's commit affirms (XD-ADR-0051)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0051)).
8. **Open the PRs**, one per repo, and list the sibling PRs in each; see
   [Make a change across repos](howto/cross-repo-change.html.md).

## What you learned

- Structure errors fail the build at once. Content changes need the change-impact report.
- Retired needs keep their ID forever, and IDs are never reused.


# tutorials/first-requirement.html.md

<a id="tut-first-requirement"></a>

# Your first requirement, end to end

#### NOTE
This tutorial is a skeleton. It is completed in Phase 5 on the real robot-arm repos.

## Goal

You follow one stakeholder need all the way down the V-model and back up to a test result:

```text
stakeholder need  <-refines-   system requirement (EARS)
                  <-satisfies- SysML part (through a generated stub)
                  <-realizes-  KiCad component (hidden TraceID field)
                  <-verifies-  test case  <-result_of-  test result
```

This is the chain the spike proved on a tiny example. Each arrow is a link that the more concrete
artifact holds ([*The concrete side holds the... (XD-RULE-0001)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0001)). Backlinks are computed by the docs build.

## Steps

The examples use the robot-arm repos. Replace the repo names with your own.

1. **Write the need and the requirement** in the requirements document of the syseng repo
   (`robarm-syseng/docs/se-req/`). Use placeholder IDs; see [Add a requirement](howto/add-a-requirement.html.md).
   ```rst
   .. sys-need:: Follow the leader arm
      :id: SYS-NEED-NEW-follow
      :category: need
      :raised_by: SYS-STH-0001

   .. sys-req:: Follow latency
      :id: SYS-REQ-NEW-latency
      :refines: SYS-NEED-NEW-follow
      :ears: ubiquitous
      :quantity: latency
      :unit: ms
      :max: 50

      The system shall move each follower joint within 50 ms of the leader joint.
   ```
2. **Issue the IDs** and build the docs, so the stubs can be made from the needs:
   ```sh
   curatrix ids fix robarm-syseng
   curatrix docs robarm-syseng
   curatrix gen stubs robarm-syseng
   ```
3. **Satisfy the requirement in the model.** Give a part definition a short-name ID and add a
   `satisfy` through the generated stub; see [Add a model element](howto/add-a-model-element.html.md). Then regenerate
   the model needs:
   ```sh
   curatrix ids fix robarm-syseng
   curatrix gen model robarm-syseng
   ```
4. **Realize the model element in a domain.** In the EE repo, give a KiCad symbol or sheet the
   hidden fields `TraceID` and `Realizes`; see [Add a PCBA or circuit block](howto/add-a-pcba.html.md). Then:
   ```sh
   curatrix gen cad-needs robarm-ee
   ```
5. **Verify it.** Write a test case that `verifies` the requirement; see
   [Add a test](howto/add-a-test.html.md). Its result becomes a test result need.
6. **Check and look.** Run the checks of each repo you touched, then build the full set:
   ```sh
   curatrix check robarm-syseng --stage local
   curatrix check robarm-ee --stage local
   curatrix docs full
   ```

   A `tracechain` table in the project overview shows the chain, and gaps are marked as
   “(missing)”.

## What can go wrong

- A link written on the wrong side, or to an unknown ID, fails the strict build ([*Link types are declared on ... (XD-RULE-0002)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0002),
  [*docs build strict (zdocs, s... (XD-CHECK-0001)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0001)).
- A model element that realizes nothing and satisfies nothing is an orphan ([*No orphan design elements (XD-RULE-0010)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0010),
  [*no orphans (R3) (XD-CHECK-0004)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0004)).
- Generated files that don’t match their sources fail the checks ([*Generated files are committ... (XD-RULE-0033)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0033)). Run the matching
  `curatrix gen` command and commit the result.

Next: [Your first change](tutorials/first-change.html.md).


# tutorials/first-workspace.html.md

<a id="tut-first-workspace"></a>

# Your first workspace

#### NOTE
This tutorial is a skeleton. It is completed in Phase 5 on the real robot-arm repos.

## Goal

You set up a workspace for one role, run the checks of one repo, and open its documents in a
browser. At the end you know where everything lives and which command does what.

## What you need

- git and Python 3.12 or newer.
- An empty folder. It becomes the **workspace root**. Every command runs from there
  ([*All commands run from the w... (XD-ADR-0060)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0060)).
- The name of the project’s manifest repo. In the examples it is `robarm-manifest`, the
  manifest of the robot-arm example.

## Steps

1. Clone the manifest repo and run its bootstrap script with your role:
   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/tiacsys/robarm-manifest
   robarm-manifest/scripts/bootstrap.sh --role syseng
   ```

   The script makes `.venv` with west, runs `west init` and `west update`, installs
   curatrix from xdmod, and then runs `curatrix bootstrap --role syseng`. The roles are listed
   in [Make a change across repos](howto/cross-repo-change.html.md) and in the workspace reference.
2. Load the workspace environment into your shell:
   ```sh
   eval "$(.venv/bin/curatrix env)"
   ```
3. Check the setup. `doctor` lists every tool with its installed and pinned version and
   fails on a mismatch:
   ```sh
   curatrix doctor
   ```
4. Run the checks of one repo. They run locally with one command ([*Every check runs locally (XD-RULE-0032)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0032)), every tool
   under a memory limit and a timeout ([*Every tool runs under limits (XD-RULE-0044)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0044)):
   ```sh
   curatrix check robarm-syseng --stage local
   ```

   The summary is in `build/robarm-syseng/checks/summary.json`. For each failure curatrix
   prints the command that reproduces it.
5. Build the documents of the repo and open them:
   ```sh
   curatrix docs robarm-syseng --open
   ```

   The HTML is in `build/robarm-syseng/docs/deploy/html/<doc-id>/`. All build output goes
   below `build/` ([*Build output only under build/ (XD-RULE-0040)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0040)).

## What you learned

- The workspace root holds `.west/`, `.venv/`, `build/` and all repos ([*One west topdir at the work... (XD-ADR-0061)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0061)).
- `curatrix` is the one command layer for people, agents and CI ([*One framework tool: curatrix (XD-ADR-0089)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0089)).
- `west update` moves repos back to their pins. While you work on branches, use
  `curatrix update` instead.

Next: [Your first requirement, end to end](tutorials/first-requirement.html.md).

# Tutorials

The tutorials walk you through XDMOD step by step. Each one starts from a clean state and ends
with a result you can see in the docs. Do them in this order.
